slice.target: Cargo offline consumption of an already-vendored directory source after repository checkout

source.lookup_query: site:doc.rust-lang.org/cargo directory sources offline cargo vendor source replacement

slice.finding: The official Cargo Book glossary defines a directory source as a set of crates stored as uncompressed files on the filesystem and points to Source Replacement for details. This confirms local-filesystem representation, but this bounded lookup did not produce official text sufficient to verify the stronger claim that an already-vendored directory source can always be consumed after checkout with zero registry/network access.
slice.verified_scope: Cargo directory sources are filesystem-resident crate sources according to the official Cargo Book glossary.
slice.not_verified_scope: Fully offline post-checkout consumption with no registry or network access; exact configuration required for source replacement; Chat-native execution of Cargo; end-to-end richer-mode parity.

scope_guard: Do not infer no-network/no-registry operation merely from filesystem residency. The stronger offline claim remains unresolved until directly documented by an official Cargo source-replacement/offline reference.
exact_continuation: On the next invocation, fresh-bootstrap and freeze current authority, then inspect exactly one official Cargo Source Replacement or Offline documentation page that directly addresses whether a configured vendored directory source eliminates registry/network access during dependency resolution/build. Preserve the distinction between local artifact transport and actual Cargo process execution; persist either direct official support or an exact unresolved blocker.
